data.gender_notes: Delmara is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek words 'delos' (visible) and 'mara' (sea). The name Delmara means 'of the sea' or 'revealed by the sea'. In Greek mythology, Delmara could refer to the goddess Delphina, who protected sailors and was said to reveal hidden treasures in the sea. The name Delmara carries the meaning “Of the sea” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Delmara usually hope their child will grow to embody of the sea and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: דלמרה
in_hebrew.meaning: אבן יקרה מן הים, תכשיט נדיר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דלמרה הוא שם שמקורו בים, אבן יקרה ונדירה, המסמלת יופי וערך רב. השם נגזר מהמילה 'דל' שפירושה אבן או חלוק, ו'מרה' שפירושה מר או יקר. יחד, השם דלמרה מייצג אבן יקרה ונדירה מן הים, המסמלת את היופי והערך הרב של הים עצמו.

in_greek.name: Δελμάρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Δελμάρα προέρχεται από τη θάλασσα, αντιπροσωπεύοντας ένα σπάνιο και πολύτιμο λίθο ή κόσμημα. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος συνδέεται με τις λέξεις 'δέλτα' που σημαίνει θάλασσα και 'μάρα' που σημαίνει σπάνιος ή πολύτιμος. Έτσι, το Δελμάρα συμβολίζει κάτι σπάνιο και πολύτιμο που προέρχεται από τη θάλασσα.

in_latin.name: Delmara
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Delmara originem in mari habet, designans lapidem rarus et pretiosum. Etymologia nominis coniungitur cum verbis 'del' quod significat lapidem et 'mara' quod significat rarus vel pretiosus. Ita, Delmara significat lapidem pretiosum et rarus e mari, symbolum pulchritudinis et valoris maris ipsius.

In the context of Christian tradition, the name Delmara represents beauty, value, and rarity, much like the sea itself. Historically, names derived from natural elements like the sea have been significant in Christian culture, often symbolizing spiritual depth and richness. The name Delmara is not directly mentioned in the Bible but carries a spiritual meaning associated with the treasures of the sea, which are often referenced in biblical scripture as symbols of wealth and divine blessings.
